title: Telescope Elasticity Prioritizer: scenario-driven RICE extension for capacity-aware roadmap scoring
creator: Maya Chen
description: Introduce the Telescope Elasticity Prioritizer (TEP): a reproducible, scenario-driven extension to RICE that folds in capacity elasticity curves, per-token cost, and latency-sensitivity profiles. TEP is designed for Redwood Inference product decisions where throughput/latency tradeoffs, Dedicated capacity commitments, and OKR alignment all matter. The prioritizer produces a composite score and a small set of actionable outputs per initiative: (1) expected per-cycle delta in cost and median latency, (2) recommended operational levers (batching, quantization, caching), and (3) risk bands across traffic/capacity scenarios.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype scoring notebook that ingests initiative R,I,C,E inputs + workload profile and outputs ranked initiatives
Monte Carlo scenario harness (traffic growth, capacity outages, pricing changes) that produces 95% and 50% risk bands for cost and latency impact
Guidance matrix mapping score ranges to recommended controls (eg. aggressive batching, hold rollout, canary at 10%)
Product-review signoff: PMs can run TEP on 3 upcoming initiatives and see ranks that reflect capacity constraints and OKR weights
decisions: Extend RICE: preserve Reach (R) and Impact (I), replace simple Confidence (C) with a two-part signal: model_confidence + execution_risk, and substitute Effort (E) with Capacity-Adjusted Cost (CAC)

Score formula: TEP_score = (R * I * Confidence_adj) / (CAC ^ elasticity_factor) where Confidence_adj = base_confidence * (1 - execution_risk) and elasticity_factor scales sensitivity to capacity constraints
Run Monte Carlo sampling across three axes: traffic distribution, capacity availability (Dedicated burst windows), and price-per-token to estimate risk bands
Prioritizer should output both a point estimate and a small matrix of recommended operational levers tied to expected economic impact
tradeoffs: Complexity vs interpretability: TEP increases inputs required (workload profile, elasticity curve) making adoption heavier than vanilla RICE but provides materially better ranking under capacity constraints
Conservative bias: putting too much weight on elasticity reduces risky high-impact initiatives in favor of low-cost ones — mitigated by OKR weighting
Data freshness: TEP requires up-to-date capacity and cost models; stale models can mis-rank work — requires scheduled model refresh cadence
implementation_steps: Draft data schema for initiative workload profile (expected QPS, 95th token length, latency sensitivity class)
Create prototype Jupyter notebook that computes TEP_score for a set of sample initiatives (link to notebook: https://confluence.redwood.com/TEP/prototype)
Integrate Monte Carlo harness using historical traffic traces (SRE to provide anonymized traces)
Create PR for a lightweight web UI prototype in Console to visualize ranked initiatives and risk bands (GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/roadmap-tep/pull/12)
Run cross-functional review (PM/Eng/SRE/Finance) and iterate scoring weights
Ship a beta to internal product teams and gather qualitative feedback over 1 cycle
metrics: Correlation with observed post-launch cost delta (target Pearson r > 0.6 on pilot initiatives)
Percent of pilot initiatives where TEP predicted correct latency risk band (within predicted 95% band) >= 80%
PM satisfaction score (internal survey) >= 4/5 after 1 pilot cycle
Time-to-score (for a given initiative) under 15 minutes once inputs are available
